The dollar amount of an interest adjustment caused by an exception event (e.g., mortgage payoff or foreclosure sale).
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies an action or step taken in the bankruptcy process.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that indicates the type of instructions from the servicer to the bankruptcy attorney on the portion of the bankruptcy proceedings the attorney is to complete on the servicer's behalf.

changeSet.Term: Bankruptcy Payment Change Notice Reason Type
changeSet.Definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason that a Payment Change Notice reflecting a change in the amount due to the servicer was filed.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the chapter of the US Bankruptcy Code under which bankruptcy has been filed.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that indicates whether the bankruptcy filed is related to personal assets or a business.
When true, indicates the bankruptcy was filed voluntarily.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the administrative standing of the bankruptcy case based upon a court ruling at a procedural milestone.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the documented status of the bankruptcy.

A mortgage with periodic installments of principal and interest that do not fully amortize the loan. The balance of the mortgage is due in a lump sum at a specified date, usually at the end of the term.
A state or local sponsored method of assisting low income borrowers and first time homeowners in the purchase of a home at a reduced interest rate.

A variable rate loan that attempts to smooth the impact of rate increases on borrowers by deferring a portion of high interest rates until maturity. Usually, all interest above a certain rate is deferred to maturity.
A loan which enables a homebuyer to get financing to make a down payment and pay closing costs on a new home before selling the present house. Also called "gap financing."
Interim financing for leased-up properties often used to repay the construction loan; typically an interest-only loan for 2 to 10 years that cannot be prepaid.
A mortgage loan which meets all requirements (size, type and age) to be eligible for purchase or securitization by federal agencies.
A short-term, interim loan for financing the cost of construction. The lender advances funds to the builder at periodic intervals as work progresses.
A short-term loan advanced before a construction loan, used by developers to acquire land and install basic utilities such as roads, sewers and water supply systems.
The final mortgage loan to the ultimate purchaser of a property, as opposed to a construction loan or other form of interim financing.
A loan made through an approved lender and insured by the Federal Housing Administration. While there are limits to the size of FHA loans, they are intended to finance moderately priced homes.
A loan originated without a firm commitment to the borrower, thereby closing at the market rate.

The portion of a mortgage loan that the lender agrees to advance without regard to the fulfillment of project leasing requirements. For example, a floor loan equaling 80% of the full amount may be funded upon completion of construction without occupancy requirements, but substantial occupancy of the building may be required for funding the full amount of the loan.
Old nickname for a VA guaranteed mortgage loan.
A loan guaranteed by a government agency or any other interested party.
Mortgage to finance an addition to or rehabilitation of a residence.
A mortgage loan secured by a residence for one, two, three or four families. Also known as a single-family mortgage, even though the property may be designed for more than one family.
A loan secured by commercial real estate.
A loan insured by FmHA, FHA or a private mortgage insurance company.
A loan made for the purpose of purchasing land only, not improvements on or to the land. Also called an "acquisition loan."
A loan for the acquisition of land to be held in anticipation of zoning, until plans are drawn and construction financing can be obtained.
A mortgage loan in which the loan amount, the loan-to-value ratio, the term or some other aspect of the loan exceeds permissible limits as specified in agency regulations.
In construction lending, interim and takeout loans made by the same investor.
A financing arrangement in which a mortgage lender receives a portion of cash flow, gross revenue or shares of ownership of a real estate venture as a part of the loan. Also called a "kicker."

A provision in a takeout commitment that requires that only a portion of permanent financing be funded on completion of construction, with the balance held back until specified occupancy levels or cash flow figures are met.
A first mortgage loan that is committed and expected to be made upon completion of a specified real estate project.

Under the Title I loan insurance program, established by Title I of the National Housing Act in 1934, lenders make loans from their own funds, and HUD insures the lender against loss if the borrower defaults on the loan. Title I loans are made for property improvement or manufactured home and lot purchase. Title I loans are also used as part of state and local community revitalization programs.
A loan to a developer secured by land being subdivided.

Mortgage loan made by an approved lender and guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs. VA loans are made to eligible veterans and those currently serving in the military, and can have a lower down payment than other types of loans.

HUD's primary program for the rehabilitation and repair of single-family properties. A 203(k) loan is a first mortgage that covers the costs of rehabilitation and purchase or refinance of an eligible property. The goals of the Section 203(k) loan program are community and neighborhood revitalization and expanded opportunities for homeownership for low- and moderate-income families.
An open-end loan, usually recorded as a second mortgage, that permits borrowers to obtain cash advances based on an approved line of credit.
Home Equity Line of Credit
Financial status ï¿½ ability of borrowers to meet the terms of their obligations.
Contains the legal disclaimer text provided by the credit bureau.

The name of the credit bureau that merges data from the credit repositories and produces credit reports for end users. The credit bureau is NOT the same as the Credit Repository (Equifax, Experian, Trans Union) that houses the raw credit files.
Identifies the software technology provider for a credit bureau, if the provider is an outside vendor.

The credit repository bureaus can identify the type of business of the liability holder or the entity requesting a credit report as listed in a credit inquiry record. This information is needed for an automated scoring application. This data is available for liability and inquiry records from Equifax, Experian and Trans Union.

This is a code value that may be associated with Credit Comment Text data. This could be a repository bureau code (Equifax, Experian, Trans Union), or it could be a code provided by a lender, credit bureau or other source that is specified in the Credit Comment Source Type. The code value should be exactly as shown in the source document without any other characters such as a prefix.
This data element provides an enumerated list of sources for the Credit Comment Code data.

changeSet.Term: Credit Comment Code Source Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit Comment Source Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.
Date the comment expires.
Indicates the date that the credit bureaus added the comment to the file of the borrower.
This data element provides an enumerated list of sources for the Credit Comment data.

This data element holds comment text data that can appear in various locations on a credit report. The Credit Comment Source Type describes the source of the comment - borrower, credit bureau, lender, or repository bureau.
Allows the credit bureau to identify the type of credit comment (e.g. Consumer Statement).
When Credit Comment Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.
This indicator is set to Y when the credit liability is being managed by a credit counseling agency.

This is a code value associated with a Credit Error Message Text element. The Credit Error Message Source Type describes the provider of the code, which could be the credit bureau, lender or the repository bureau.
Specifies the source of an error message. Messages can come either from the credit data repository, lender or the credit bureau.

This is error message text that appears in a credit response transaction. It may be accompanied by a Credit Error Message Source Type that describes the source of the error message text. It may also be accompanied by a Credit Error Message Code value that refers to the error message text.

changeSet.Term: Credit File Borrower Age Years Count
changeSet.Definition: The age of the borrower reported in the credit file returned from the repository bureau. The age is sometimes reported in lieu of the date of birth.
The Infile Date is the date that the credit data repository first established this credit data file on this borrower.
The identification number of the credit bureau that owns or manages the credit file being referenced.
The name of the credit bureau that owns or manages the credit file being referenced.

Describes the resulting status of the request for a credit file from a credit repository bureau. The full reason for a Credit File not being returned will be reported in the Credit Error Message data element.

changeSet.Term: Credit File Result Status Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit File Result Status Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.

This element indicates that there was a variation from the original borrower demographics data in the request and the borrower data in the credit file. It MAY or MAY NOT belong to the borrower specified in the credit request.

The Personal Identification Number (PIN) that is supplied by the credit data repository bureau (Equifax, Experian, Trans Union) to allow a lender to access a credit file that was previously "frozen" or locked at the request of the borrower.
The date of the credit inquiry.
The result from a credit inquiry - did the lender offer credit, refuse credit, etc.
The number of times the liability account was reported 120 days late by the liability holder.
The number of times the liability account was reported 30 days late by the liability holder.
The number of times the liability account was reported 60 days late by the liability holder.
The number of times the liability account was reported 90 days late by the liability holder.
The date that the reported Credit Liability Unpaid Balance Amount was reached.
The date that the credit liability account was closed by the liability holder (by either the borrower or the liability holder).
The account number assigned to the liability account as provided by the credit repository bureau.
The date that the credit liability account was opened by the liability holder.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the ownership relation of the borrower(s) to the liability account (i.e. are they solely responsible, jointly responsible, a co-signer on the account, etc.).
The date that the credit liability was reported paid to zero by the liability holder.
The date that the credit liability data was reported by the liability holder.

The Status Date is the date that the accounts Current Rating was changed to that status by the liability holder. If the Current Rating status is Bankruptcy, for example, the Status Date would be when the account first went into bankruptcy.
This data element is an enumerated status list for an account as of the Account Status Date.
This describes the type of account established with the Liability Account Holder - credit line, installment, mortgage, open, revolving).
The actual dollar amount received on the borrower's liability account as recorded by the liability holder, for period specified on the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.
The amount that will be due on the account in the form a lump sum balloon payment.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Balloon Payment Due Date
changeSet.Definition: According to the contract / invoice, the date that full payment is due on an account.
The amount charged off by a liability holder, usually for an account in collection.
The date that the creditor put the account in a "charge off " status and declared the account balance as uncollectable.
A description of any collateral for the loan (for example, 97 Corvette).
This element indicates whether or not the consumer (borrower) disputes information reported for this account and has filed a FCRA (Fair Credit Reporting Act) dispute document.
The maximum amount of credit extended to the borrower as of the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.

The liability accounts current code (as of Date Reported) for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account. This is also known as the Manner Of Payment (MOP). See the MISMO Implementation Guide: Credit Reporting for more information on MOP codes.
The liability accounts current rating (as of Date Reported) for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account.
This element indicates whether or not the liability account contains adverse or derogatory information.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability First Reported Default Date
changeSet.Definition: The date the loan was first reported to the credit bureau with a status code indicating bankruptcy or 30 day delinquency.
The highest amount of unpaid credit ever recorded on the liability as of the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Highest Adverse Rating Amount
changeSet.Definition: The highest delinquent amount on the account as reported by the liability holder.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Highest Adverse Rating Code
changeSet.Definition: The liability accounts highest (or worst) rating code for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account. This is also known as the Manner Of Payment or MOP code. See the MISMO Implementation Guide: Credit Reporting for more information on MOP codes.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Highest Adverse Rating Date
changeSet.Definition: The date of the highest (worst) delinquency reported by the liability holder.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Highest Adverse Rating Type
changeSet.Definition: The liability accounts highest (or worst) rating type for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account.
The date of last account activity, such as last charge or last payment, as of the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.
The date of the last payment on the liability reported by the liability holder.
This element indicates whether or not the data in the liability account has been manually updated by the credit bureau based on an investigation.

The dollar amount of the monthly payment required on borrower's liability account as reported on a credit report. The amount is either calculated by the credit bureau or provided by the credit liability holder.
The number of months from the Credit Liability Account Reported Date that are remaining to be paid on an installment loan account.
The number of months of account history reported by the liability holder. This is the period over which Late Counts are accumulated.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Most Recent Adverse Rating Amount
changeSet.Definition: The most recent amount that the borrower was reported delinquent by the liability holder.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Most Recent Adverse Rating Code
changeSet.Definition: The liability accounts most recent delinquency rating code for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account. See the MISMO Implementation Guide: Credit Reporting for more information on MOP codes.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Most Recent Adverse Rating Date
changeSet.Definition: The date of the most recent delinquency reported by the liability holder.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Most Recent Adverse Rating Type
changeSet.Definition: The liability accounts most recent delinquency rating type for how timely the borrower has been making payments on this account.
When a liability account has been transferred or is being handled by a collection agency, this element indicates the name of original creditor.
The past due amount of credit owed by the borrower as of the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Payment Pattern Data Text
changeSet.Definition: This is a set of previous monthly payment ratings beginning with the Payment Pattern Start Date. C=Current, 1-6=# Months Late, 7=Wage Earner Plan, 8=Repossession, 9=Collection, N=No Activity, X=No Data.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Payment Pattern Start Date
changeSet.Definition: The date of the beginning of the data in the Credit Liability Payment Pattern Data.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Prior Adverse Rating Code
changeSet.Definition: This is the accounts Manner Of Payment (MOP) rating code for the associated Prior Adverse Rating Date. See the MISMO Implementation Guide: Credit Reporting for more information on MOP codes.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Prior Adverse Rating Date
changeSet.Definition: Lists the date (month and year) that the borrower was late on payments. The associated Prior Adverse Rating element gives the rating for that date.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Prior Adverse Rating Type
changeSet.Definition: This is the accounts manner Of payment rating type for the associated Prior Adverse Rating Date.

changeSet.Term: Credit Liability Prior Information Start Date
changeSet.Definition: The start date of the most recent populated Credit Liability Prior Information record.
A text description for the loan terms (for example, 360 months at $820 per month).
The total number of months established as terms for repayment of a loan.
This enumerated element indicates whether the monthly payment terms amount was provided by the repository bureau, or calculated by the credit bureau.
The unpaid amount of credit owed by the borrower as of the Credit Liability Account Reported Date.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Account Ownership Type
changeSet.Definition: Describes the ownership relation of the borrower(s) to the public record (i.e. are they individually responsible, jointly responsible, terminated).
The name of the attorney (normally the plaintiff) reported in the public record.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Consumer Dispute Indicator
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates whether or not the consumer (borrower) disputes information reported for this public record and has filed a FCRA (Fair Credit Reporting Act) dispute document.
The name of the court reporting the public record.
The name of the defendant in a public record.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Derogatory Data Indicator
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates whether or not the public record contains adverse or derogatory information.
This element provides the date that the Public Record Disposition Type first became effective.

This is the enumerated disposition or the public record as of the Disposition Date. If the disposition does not fit one of the enumerated categories, select Other, and enter it in the Credit Public Record Disposition Type Other Description element.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Disposition Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: If the Credit Public Record Disposition Type is set to Other, enter the disposition in this element.
The Docket Identifier can be a Case Number, Docket Number, Public Record Book, Page or Sequence Number.
The date that the public record was filed by the court.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Legal Obligation Amount
changeSet.Definition: This is the amount listed in the public record that the defendant is obligated to pay.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Manual Update Indicator
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates whether or not the data in the public record has been manually updated by the credit bureau based on an investigation.
The date that the Legal Obligation Amount was paid to zero.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Payment Frequency Type
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates the frequency of payments allowed for the Legal Obligation Amount.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Payment Frequency Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected for Credit Public Record Payment Frequency Type.
The name of the plaintiff in a public record.
The date that the public record data was last reported by the court to the credit repository bureau.
The date that the public record case was settled.

This is the enumerated type of public record reported by the credit bureau. If the type does not fit one of the enumerated categories, enter the type in the Credit Public Record Type Other Description element.

changeSet.Term: Credit Public Record Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: If the Public Record Type is set to Other, enter the type in this element.
A rating given to a person or company that establishes creditworthiness based upon present financial condition, experience and past credit history.

Identifies which system of Manner Of Payment (MOP) rating codes is in the credit report. If Other is selected, then the name of the coding system will appear in the Credit Rating Code Type Other Description.

changeSet.Term: Credit Rating Code Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: If the Credit Rating Code Type is set to Other, enter its description in this data attribute.
Specifies the type of credit history or type of payments used as credit history to establish acceptable credit reputation.
A free-form text field used to capture the Credit Reference Type if Other is selected.

1) A report run by an independent credit agency which verifies certain information concerning an applicantâ€™s credit standing 2) Describes the borrowers credit history. Provided by a credit reporting bureau, or a service which consolidates reports from multiple sources into a single report (Tri-merge). AKA: Tri-Merge, Residential Mortgage Credit Report (RMCR).
Indicates that the borrower gave the lender consent to pull credit report.
Date and time the referenced credit report was first issued.
A reference number assigned by the credit bureau to a specific credit report. This report number is also referenced when a Reissue, Upgrade, or Status Query of an existing report is requested.
The date and time that the referenced credit report was last updated or revised.
This element indicates how duplicate data from multiple sources is handled on a credit report.
The price of the credit report produced on the borrower(s).
This describes the type of the Credit Report Price (Net, Tax, Total or Other). If Other is selected enter the description into the Credit Report Price Type Other Description element.

changeSet.Term: Credit Report Price Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Other is specified in Price Type, this element contains its description.
This is additional information that more completely describes the credit report product being requested.
Select the type of service action being requested. If the service action refers to an existing report, specify which one in the Credit Report Identifier.

changeSet.Term: Credit Report Request Action Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: This describes the desired request action when the Credit Report Request Action Type is set to Other.
Uniquely identifies a specific instance of a credit report transaction.

The type of credit report that was requested or produced. Most common types are Merged report (data from credit data repositories is merged), and RMCR (Residential Mortgage Credit Report - contains verified liabilities, employment, etc.).
When Credit Report Type is set to Other, enter its description in this element.

This element stores the number of repository bureaus desired for a credit request. When a requestor uses this element, they are selecting the number of repositories to be pulled, not specific bureaus. The credit bureau would then choose which bureaus to be pulled based on a methodology agreed on with their customer (for example, zip code or customer preference).
This element indicates whether Equifax is included in either the request or response.
This element indicates whether Experian is included in either the request or response.

changeSet.Term: Credit Repository Included Other Repository Name
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates whether another repository source is included in either the request or response.

changeSet.Term: Credit Repository Included Trans Union Indicator
changeSet.Definition: This element indicates whether Trans Union is included in either the request or response.
If true, indicates the credit report was based on the input from a single credit repository. Also known as a single in-file credit report.
Indicates whether a Credit Repository Source is available. If a Credit Repository Source is available then the source can be provided in Credit Repository Source Type.
This element describes the source of the credit file, Equifax, Experian, Trans Union or Unspecified if the specific sources are not specified.

changeSet.Term: Credit Repository Source Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit Repository Source Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.
This is the subscriber code (sometimes called member code) of the liability holder or provider of data to the credit repository bureau.
A system generated date and time stamp enclosed within each request to identify the initiation time of the credit request.
The Credit Request Type specifies either an Individual Report on one person, or a Joint Report on two married persons.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Adverse Indicator
changeSet.Definition: This indicator is set to Y when the Credit Response Alert Message contains information which may be considered adverse and may require further investigation or other action.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Category Type
changeSet.Definition: Describes the general category of the alert message. This allows for automated processing by systems reading the credit alert messages.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Category Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit Response Alert Message Category Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.
This is the code value associated with the Credit Response Alert Message Text and/or Credit Response Alert Message Type.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Code Source Type
changeSet.Definition: This element identifies the name of the source for the code values used in the Credit Response Alert Message Code. The enumeration definition identifies the source document and name of the table that contains the code values.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Code Source Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When the Credit Response Alert Message Code Source Type has a value of Other, this element identifies the name of the source for the code values used in the Credit Response Alert Message Code.
Text of the alert message.
Lists the name of the repository bureau or other product that generated the alert message.

changeSet.Term: Credit Response Alert Message Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit Response Alert Message Type is set to Other, enter its value in this data element.

An enumerated list that describes the general type or purpose of a credit score model. This allows LOS systems to extract scores by a more general category, without having to know the specific score model names.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Category Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When Credit Score Category Type is set to "Other", enter its value in this data element.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents a specific version, release of a Credit Score Category Type.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Category Version Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Credit Score Category Version Type.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Considered In Decision Indicator
changeSet.Definition: When true, indicates borrower's credit score was obtained from a consumer reporting agency and the score was used in making the credit decision.
Date that the referenced credit score was produced.
A value from a MISMO defined list that identifies the reason why a credit score could not be generated.

This indicator is set to True when the Credit Risk Score Value of the borrower or guarantor was negatively affected by the presence of credit inquiry records on their credit report. There may be FACT Act compliance requirements related to this alert message.

Factors of the borrower's or guarantor's credit which give context to the referenced credit score. The factor is normally a numeric code. The Credit Score Factor Text contains the text for the factor code.
The text remarks associated with a Credit Score Factor

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Histogram Interval High Value
changeSet.Definition: The highest possible value for the score model within the given credit score histogram interval.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Histogram Interval Low Value
changeSet.Definition: The lowest possible value for the score model within the given credit score histogram interval.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Histogram Interval Score Range Occurrence Percent
changeSet.Definition: The percent of consumers that have score values within this credit score histogram interval.
This is the upper range of possible score values for this Credit Score Model Name Type. The range of credit score values is required to be part of the FACTA disclosure.
This is the lower range of possible score values for this Credit Score Model Name Type. The range of credit score values is required to be part of the FACTA disclosure.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the score algorithm model name used to produce the referenced credit risk score.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Model Name Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: When the Credit Score Model Name Type is set to Other, this element holds the description.

changeSet.Term: Credit Score Model Range of Scores Description
changeSet.Definition: The range of scores possible under the credit score model.
Identifies the name of the company providing the credit score data. This is one of the requirements of the 2003 FACT Act.
Specifies the URL or web site address of the company providing the credit score data.
A detailed description of how the credit score compares to the scores of other consumers.
The percentile that the parties credit score is in comparison to all consumers.
Numeric credit score resulting from credit evaluation model.

The Credit Summary Data Set Name-Value pair data provides a standard method of providing a set of summary data. The Data Set Name identifies the type of summary data. The Data Set Value contains the actual data described by the Data Set Name.
This element holds the actual data value described by the Credit Summary Data Set Name attribute.
This is the name used to label or describe an individual group of summary data elements. It is useful when there are multiple groups of summary data elements within a credit report.
Any type of additional summary data that is provided by the credit bureau.

Informs the borrower that a consumer report is used in connection with providing credit with materially less favorable terms than the most favorable terms available to a substantial proportion of customers.
The name of the party that has been identified as an Additional End-User of credit report data by the party requesting the credit report data.

Informs the borrower of their credit score, range of possible scores, key factors affecting score, reporting agencies used, contacts for obtaining a report copy, and includes a statement that terms offered are based on consumer report information.
When true, indicates the credit liability is currently in forbearance.
When true, indicates that the loan is a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC).
Confirms borrower credit information. AKA: VOC.
A free-form text field used to describe or reconcile the different approaches to value and the data used to arrive at the final property valuation.
When true, indicates that a factory-built certification is present and has been examined for a modular home.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason an assumption request was denied.

changeSet.Term: Assumption Denial Reason Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is used for AssumptionDenialReasonType.
The date associated with the specified AssumptionStatusType.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the current status of the assumption.
A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when Other is used for AssumptionStatusType.
The date the former obligor is officially released from loan payment obligations.
When true, the servicer does not report to credit bureaus based on the value provided in Credit Ineligible Description.
A free-form text field describing the reason that the borrower is ineligible for credit reporting.
The date that the loan is reported to credit bureaus as terminated.
The date associated with the specified PropertyCurrentOccupancyType.
The sum of all past due principal from the last paid installment due date (DDLPI) to the current date. It is computed based on scheduled amortization.

changeSet.Term: Total Delinquent Tax And Insurance Amount
changeSet.Definition: The sum of all past due real estate taxes and insurance premiums from previous scheduled monthly payments to the current date.
The sum of all past due amounts from previous scheduled monthly payments to the current date that do not pertain to PITI.
The amount of principal or amounts capitalized to principal deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
The amount of the escrow balance deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
The amount of borrower corporate advances deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven.
The amount of all other funds deferred until future repayment is due or balance is forgiven. This may include late charges and fees.

changeSet.Term: Government Agency Conditional Commitment Issue Date
changeSet.Definition: The date on which a conditional commitment for guaranty is issued by the government agency.
The date USDA issued the Loan Note Guarantee confirming a promise to pay in the event of borrower default.
Specifies the type of SCRA relief that the borrower is receiving.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the SCRAReliefType.
The date on which SCRA benefits, such as interest rate reductions and/or foreclosure protections, begin to apply to the loan.
The date on which SCRA benefits, such as interest rate reductions and/or foreclosure protections end.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the investor holding the first mortgage.

changeSet.Term: First Mortgage Holder Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for FirstMortgageHolderType.
The amount of the remaining partial claim balance after applying the most recent payment supplement amount from the partial claim subsidy account.
The amount of the monthly payment that represents funds for the payment supplement account subsidy that is part of the total payment being reported.
The date that a portion of the secured property was released from the lien.

changeSet.Term: Partial Release Of Security Due To Eminent Domain Indicator
changeSet.Definition: When true, indicates that the reason for the partial release of security is eminent domain.
When true, indicates that at the time of conveyance, the property meets all acceptable conveyance conditions defined by the agency or investor.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that represents the registration status of a vacant property with the applicable municipality.

changeSet.Term: Property Vacancy Registration Status Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the PropertyVacancyRegistrationStatusType.
The date associated with the specified PropertyVacancyRegistrationStatusType.
An unstructured name that identifies the municipality where the vacant property has been registered.

changeSet.Term: Property Preservation Action Type Additional Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to provide a supplemental comment or remark regarding the PropertyPreservationActionType.
A free-form text field used to further describe taxes paid to a tax authority.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the source of the comment.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the status of the successor in interest.

changeSet.Term: Successor In Interest Status Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is used for SuccessorInInterestStatusType.
The date associated with the specified SuccessorInInterestStatusType.

changeSet.Term: Successor In Interest Ownership Aquisition Reason Type
changeSet.Definition: A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the reason the successor in interest has acquired ownership rights to the property.

changeSet.Term: Successor In Interest Ownership Aquisition Reason Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is used for SuccessorInInterestOwnershipAcquisitionReasonType.

changeSet.Term: Successor In Interest Legal Ownership In Property Effective Date
changeSet.Definition: The date that the ownership in the subject property was effective for the specified successor in interest.
When true, indicates that the borrower is ineligible for year end IRS reporting (e.g., IRS Form 1098 or applicable IRS Forms 1099).
A free-form text field describing the reason that the borrower is ineligible for year end IRS reporting.
The date on which a Social Security Number has been verified as authorized by the Borrower using Form SSA-89.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that describes the result of the trial payment plan.

changeSet.Term: Trial Plan Result Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field used to capture additional information when Other is selected for TrialPlanResultType.
The date that the deed in lieu of foreclosure was recorded with the local government office.

changeSet.Term: Deed In Lieu Recording Submission Date
changeSet.Definition: The date that the deed in lieu of foreclosure was submitted for recordation with the local government office.
The fair market value of the property minus reasonable costs associated with the transaction or a cost factor defined by investor guidelines.
The amount of the partial claim submitted by the servicer to the government agency.
The dollar amount of the partial claim that was paid by the guarantor to the servicer.
The date on which the partial claim note and mortgage were executed by the borrower.

changeSet.Term: Partial Claim Original UPB Used In Calculation Percent
changeSet.Definition: A portion of 100 that represents the percentage of the original unpaid principal balance used to calculate the partial claim.

A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the type of partial claim that is being requested. Partial Claims may eliminate the arrearage amount and bring the loan current and/or provide payment relief through a principal reduction or payment subsidy.
A free-form text field used to collect additional information when Other is selected as the PartialClaimType.

changeSet.Term: Partial Claim Payment Subsidy Effective Date
changeSet.Definition: The date the partial claim payment subsidy becomes effective to reduce the borrower's payment.

changeSet.Term: Partial Claim Payment Subsidy End Date
changeSet.Definition: The date the partial claim payment subsidy ends and the borrower no longer receives a payment reduction.
The dollar amount by which the UPB was reduced as a result of the partial claim amount.
When true indicates that the communication is about the borrower's dissatisfaction with the Servicer or other entity related to their mortgage.
When true, indicates that the winning bid at the foreclosure sale was submitted by a party other than the servicer.
A value from a MISMO prescribed list that specifies the purpose of obtaining a Certificate of Eligibility.

changeSet.Term: Certificate Of Eligibility Use Type Other Description
changeSet.Definition: A free-form text field that specifies the enumeration when the value of Other is used for Certificate of Eligibility of Use Type.

changeSet.Term: VA Dependency And Indemnity Compensation Indicator
changeSet.Definition: When true, indicates receipt of Dependency and Indemnity Compensation - a monthly, tax-free benefit for survivors of deceased veterans.

Process in which the Servicer follows the mandatory, hierarchical sequence of steps to evaluate borrowers who are in default or imminent risk of default for options to avoid foreclosure. Also referred to as the Default Waterfall.

A mortgage banking function responsible for developing mortgage products to originate, managing interest rate risk, setting pricing, and executing the sale, securitization, or retention of mortgage loans in a way that optimizes liquidity, profitability, and balance sheet efficiency.
Process in which the Lender determines what loan products to offer based on market conditions, business strategy, and investor demand.
Process in which the Lender sets interest rates based on market conditions, business strategy, and investor demand.
Process in which the Lender uses financial strategies to preserve margin and protect from interest rate fluctuations before loans are sold.
Process in which the Lender oversees the flow of loans from origination to sale, ensuring locks are managed, extensions are handled, and loans are delivered efficiently.
Process in which the Lender administers lock policies, facilitates inquiries, and remediates issues related to lock commitments through the end-to-end lifecycle of interest rate locks.
Process in which the Lender engages with approved counterparties to obtain investor commitments to purchase individual or pools of loans, pursuant to applicable commitment types.
Process in which the Lender monitors locked and closed pipeline for the identification of commitment modifications to achieve good delivery through pair-offs, upsizing, or extensions.
Process in which the Lender analyzes and reports on delivery performance, including the reason for fallout.
Process of validating that the Title Agent is in good standing with the Title Underwriter and that the financial aspects of the transaction are within the Title Agent's allowed limits.

The process in which the Lender validates that the Title and/or Settlement Agent(s) are in good standing with the Title Underwriter and/or appropriate regulator and that the financial aspects of the transaction are within the Title and/or Settlement Agent's allowed limits.

Process of obtaining a Title Insurance Policy to ensure that the necessary and proper ownership rights are established when real estate is conveyed from one party to another. Title is ordered to confirm lien position and protect ownership interest.

The process in which the Lender initiates the necessary actions for conducting the closing and ensuring that title to the property meets the requirements of the parties. These actions may include a title search, issuance of a Title Commitment or Preliminary Report, a Closing Protection Letter (CPL), clearing title, overseeing the execution of documents, post closing settlement actions, and issuance of the Loan and Owner Title Policies.
The process in which the consumer considers the flood risk of a property.
The process in which the consumer considers the hazard risk of a property.

The process of analyzing the Environmental, Social, and Governance impacts of a loan/security to ensure the sustainability and ethical impact of the investment. Also includes the ongoing review of the company's internal policies and procedures for compliance with industry ESG best practices.

changeSet.Term: Address Housing Emerging Risks and Opportunities
changeSet.Definition: The process of addressing housing emerging risks and opportunities.
Processes that are done in support of normal operations but are outside of the loan lifecycle.
An interim loan given to finance the difference between the floor loan and the maximum permanent loan as committed. Also called bridge financing.

One of Fannie Maeï¿½s major tools for neighborhood and community revitalization, the HomeStyle Second Mortgage is designed for home-buyers or homeowners at all income levels who wish to repair, remodel, enlarge or substantially renovate a home. Introduced in 1993, this program was designed to help lenders capture the growing U.S. market for home remodeling.
A loan arrangement wherein the lender shares in property income as well as interest earned on the loan.
Programs that subsidize the market interest rate on mortgage loans, thus lowering the consumerï¿½s housing cost.
Financing used from the beginning of a project to the closing of a permanent loan. Usually a construction or development loan.
A mortgage which is larger than the legislated purchase limits of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
A loan made for the purpose of purchasing land only, not improvements on or to the land. Also called an "acquisition loan."

Mortgage insurance program which allows the lender to collect a higher interest rate from the borrower and forward the excess interest to the mortgage insurance company to pay for the mortgage insurance.

Ability to Repay (ATR) requires that a lender make a reasonable, good-faith determination before or when consummating a mortgage loan that the consumer has a reasonable ability to repay the loan, considering such factors as the consumerï¿½s income or assets and employment status

The part of a Web page that is visible once the page has loaded ï¿½ normally the top part. This term is pertinent to the electronic mortgage world as E-sign requires the presentation of documents to be compliant with state statutes that govern font, pagination, format etc.

A stipulation within the regulatory acts governing the investments of insurance companies, savings and loan associations and mutual savings banks, allowing for a small percentage of total assets to be placed in investments not otherwise permitted by the acts.
State laws covering the registration and sale of new securities.

An agreement wherein the borrower/guarantor has personally agreed to fully repay all amounts owed under a mortgage loan, irrespective of whether the collateral is adequate to retire the debt. This agreement gives the holder of the note, or other negotiable instrument, the right to recover against the borrower/guarantor personally, including any and all assets of the borrower/ guarantor.

An agreement wherein the borrower/guarantor has personally agreed to repay a set dollar amount, all amounts exceeding a stated dollar amount or a percentage of the outstanding balance of the mortgage loan. This agreement gives the holder of the note, or other negotiable instrument, the right to recover against the borrower/guarantor personally, including any and all assets of the borrower/guarantor, but only to the extent specified. For example, a borrower/guarantor may agree to pay the first $1 million of a $5 million loan or the top 25% of the loan.
Regulations based on safety and health standards that govern design, construction and materials used in construction.
Coastal Barrier Reform Act

Under Title 1 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, eight former categorical grant and loan programs were replaced by a system of unified block grants under which communities of over 50,000 people are entitled to receive funding, while other communities may apply for discretionary funding. Its purpose is to encourage more broadly conceived community development projects and expand housing opportunities for low- and moderate-income persons.
In some states, a form of ownership under which property acquired during a marriage is presumed to be owned jointly unless acquired as separate property of either spouse.
Federal legislation which requires every financial institution to help meet the credit needs of its entire community, including low- and moderate-income neighborhoods.
Adopted in 1974, the Act affects many aspects of pension and profit-sharing plans, and regulates the investments such plans can make and the conduct of their fiduciaries.

A federal law that requires lenders and other creditors to make credit equally available without discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status or receipt of income from public assistance programs. Also called "Regulation B."

The common law right to redeem property following default on a mortgage by paying the unpaid debt plus interest and costs prior to the foreclosure sale. In some states, the mortgagor has a statutory right to redeem property after a foreclosure sale.

Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act. On June 30, 2000, Congress enacted this Act to facilitate the use of electronic records and signatures in interstate and foreign commerce by ensuring the validity and legal effect of contracts entered into electronically.
ESIGN and UETA.
Fair And Accurate Credit Transaction Act
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act
Federal legislation empowering state and local governments to issue tax-free bonds to fund mortgages for low- and middle-income borrowers.

changeSet.Term: Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery and Enforcement Act (FIRREA)
changeSet.Definition: The law enacted to restructure the thrift industry. The Act created regulatory entities to oversee thrifts and established risk-based capital guidelines for Qualified Thrift Lenders (QTLs). The Act created the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS), the Federal Housing Finance Board (FHFB) and the Resolution Trust Corporation (RTC); the Act dissolved the Federal Home Loan Bank Board (FHLBB) and the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation (FSLIC).
A framework of accounting standards, rules and procedures defined by the professional accounting industry, which has been adopted by nearly all publicly traded U.S. companies.

The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, otherwise known as the Financial Modernization Act of 1999, requires companies to give consumers privacy notices that explain the institutionsï¿½ information-sharing practices. In turn, consumers have the right to limit some ï¿½ but not all ï¿½ sharing of their information.
Regulations or guidelines used as underwriting criteria that set forth acceptable property standards and specifications.
A home loan that meets standards set forth by the federal government that prohibit or limit certain high-risk products and features.
Federal Reserve regulation prohibiting discrimination against consumer credit applicants, and establishing guidelines for collecting and evaluating credit information.
Regulation written by the Federal Reserve Board to implement the Truth-in-Lending Act, requiring full written disclosure of the credit portion of a purchase, including the annual percentage rate.
Places restrictions upon governmental authorities having access to copies of the financial records of any mortgage applicant.
Rules established by the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS) which dictate how much of certain types of capital a savings and loan may hold.

On July 30, 2002, President Bush signed into law the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, which he characterized as ""the most far reaching reforms of American business practices since the time of Franklin Delano Roosevelt."" The Act mandated a number of reforms to enhance corporate responsibility, enhance financial disclosures and combat corporate and accounting fraud, and created the ""Public Company Accounting Oversight Board,"" also known as the PCAOB, to oversee the activities of the auditing profession.

changeSet.Term: Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act (SAFE Act)
changeSet.Definition: Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage Licensing Act (SAFE Act)
State laws requiring that certain contracts be in writing; including contracts for the sale of real property.
UCC is drafted by the Uniform Law Commission and the American Law Institute.

Uniform Electronic Transaction Act. A uniform form of statute that various states have enacted to establish the legal validity and enforceability of electronic signatures, contracts, and other records within the enforcing state. This term is also defined in the MERSï¿½ eRegistry Procedures Manual available at members.mersinc.org.
